summary: Russian forces carried out a large‑scale strike on Crimea and Sevastopol energy infrastructure, causing a temporary blackout. Ukraine reports increased ballistic missile launches toward Kyiv and its suburbs amid interceptor shortages. Both sides continue intensive UAV activity across multiple fronts.
key_points: Russian forces struck energy facilities in Crimea and Sevastopol, temporarily cutting electricity and forcing backup power use (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405).
Ukrainian officials warn of a possible surge in ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv and its suburbs due to a shortage of air‑defence interceptors (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68622).
U.S. intelligence warns Russia may conduct at least two mass combined strikes on Kyiv within the next ten days (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68627).
Multiple Shahed loitering munitions were launched from Chauda (Crimea), Bryansk and Donetsk regions, with 5‑10, 2‑4, and 1‑2 units respectively (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68629).
Ukrainian gas stations in Poltava, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions have been attacked repeatedly, though authorities say fuel supplies remain stable (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31429).
A Nova Poshta logistics centre in Kyiv’s Obolonsky district and another terminal in Zaporizhzhia were destroyed by Russian strikes (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31419).
Ukrainian air‑defence failed to intercept a ballistic missile during an overnight attack, prompting Zelensky to request Patriot systems at the NATO summit (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31408).
Ukrainian UAVs reported over the Black Sea and near the Crimean peninsula, including two Orion drones operating simultaneously (Source: @eRadarrua/99938).

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces carried out a large‑scale strike on Crimea and Sevastopol energy infrastructure, causing a temporary blackout. Ukraine warns of a possible surge in ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv and its suburbs amid interceptor shortages. Both sides continue intensive UAV activity across multiple fronts.

points: Zelensky appealed for Patriot missiles after an overnight attack where Ukrainian air‑defences failed to intercept a ballistic missile, emphasizing the need for interceptor supplies at the NATO summit in Ankara (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31408).

Ukrainian officials reported attacks on approximately 100 gas stations over the past month, with recent strikes in Poltava, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions, though local authorities say fuel shortages are not expected (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31429).

The Russian Armed Forces destroyed a Nova Poshta logistics centre in Kyiv’s Obolonsky district and a terminal in Zaporizhzhia, targeting postal and supply infrastructure (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31419).
Ukrainian UAV activity was observed over the Black Sea and near the Crimean peninsula, including two Orion drones operating simultaneously (Source: @eRadarrua/99938).

Russian forces launched a massive strike on Crimea and Sevastopol energy facilities, temporarily cutting power and forcing backup generators, while also targeting civilian maritime vessels in the Sea of Azov (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405).
Shahed loitering munitions were launched from Chauda (Crimea) (5‑10 units), Bryansk (2‑4 units) and Donetsk (1‑2 units) toward Ukrainian targets (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68629).
A Tu‑160 bomber, likely equipped with Kh‑101 cruise missiles, departed Engels airfield and was reported to be relocating to the Ukrainian‑controlled “Ukrainka” airfield (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68628).
Russian intelligence reportedly obtained a Ukrainian GUR smartphone for an amount equal to a monthly salary, according to TASS (Source: @tass_agency/384033).

Ukrainian sources reported a Russian strike on a logistics centre in the Obolonsky district of Kyiv and another terminal in Zaporizhzhia, indicating continued pressure on eastern supply lines (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31419).
UAV activity was noted moving from Sumy toward Hadiach in Poltava region, suggesting reconnaissance or strike missions along the eastern axis (Source: @kpszsu/67509).
Russian forces claimed to have destroyed a Ukrainian UAV targeting a power substation in the Kursk region, though Ukrainian reports do not confirm (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31412).

Reports of Russian assault troops engaging in small‑arms battles in Shostka district (Sumy) and villages such as Bachevsk and Pisarevka indicate ongoing ground combat on the eastern front (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405).
Ukrainian UAVs were observed north of Sumy heading toward the Chernihiv region, indicating surveillance activity near the northern front (Source: @kpszsu/67570).
Multiple Shahed launches were reported from Bryansk and Donetsk, potentially targeting northern approaches to Kyiv (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68629).
UAVs were detected moving from the north of Chernihiv toward the regional centre, suggesting possible strike preparation (Source: @kpszsu/67575).
A ballistic missile was reported over Kyiv from the direction of Chernihiv, heading toward the Lisovyi forest and Darnytsia districts (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68604).
Ukrainian UAVs were observed moving northward from the Black Sea toward Odesa and from the sea toward Mykolaiv, indicating southern maritime surveillance (Source: @kpszsu/67538).
Russian strikes hit two gas stations in Zaporizhzhia and at least one in Mykolaiv region, showing continued targeting of southern logistics (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31424).

A Russian long‑range precision strike targeted fuel and energy facilities in Kyiv and the Kyiv region, as well as a military airfield in Dnipropetrovsk, reflecting southern‑to‑central strike capability (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31412).
UAV activity was reported over the Black Sea, with two Orion drones operating, potentially supporting southern operations (Source: @eRadarrua/99938).
Ukrainian air‑defence failed to intercept a ballistic missile during an overnight attack, prompting urgent requests for Patriot systems (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31408).
More than 70 UAVs were shot down over Yaroslavl region while attempting to attack an oil refinery, indicating high UAV activity in the broader theater (Source: @tass_agency/384040).
Russian forces employed long‑range precision‑guided weapons launched from land, air and sea, targeting military‑industrial sites and energy facilities across Ukraine (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31412).
A Tu‑160 bomber, likely armed with Kh‑101 cruise missiles, was observed relocating from Engels to “Ukrainka,” suggesting potential strike missions (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68628).

key_developments: Large‑scale Russian strike on Crimea and Sevastopol energy infrastructure caused temporary blackout, highlighting vulnerability of Russian‑occupied territories (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405).
U.S. intelligence warns of at least two mass combined Russian strikes on Kyiv within ten days, indicating imminent high‑intensity attacks (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68627).
Zelensky’s request for Patriot missiles after a failed ballistic missile interception underscores critical interceptor shortages (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31408).
Shahed loitering munitions launched from multiple Russian regions (Crimea, Bryansk, Donetsk) show diversified attack vectors (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68629).
Repeated attacks on Ukrainian gas stations across several regions could strain civilian fuel supplies despite official assurances (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31429).
Destruction of Nova Poshta logistics centres in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia disrupts Ukrainian supply chains (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31419).
Ukrainian UAV activity over the Black Sea and near Crimea indicates ongoing reconnaissance and potential strike preparation (Source: @eRadarrua/99938).
sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces are intensifying long‑range strike capabilities, employing both ballistic missiles and cruise‑armed bombers, while increasing Shahed loitering munition launches from multiple directions. Ukraine faces critical interceptor shortages, limiting its ability to counter ballistic threats, and its logistics infrastructure is under pressure from targeted strikes on fuel and postal facilities. Continued UAV activity across all fronts suggests sustained reconnaissance and potential escalation of kinetic operations.
sections.regional_response: Ukrainian authorities are urging heightened civil defence measures in Kyiv, including sheltering and air‑raid alerts, while seeking accelerated delivery of Patriot systems from NATO partners. Regional administrations report no immediate fuel shortages despite repeated attacks on gas stations, aiming to maintain civilian morale. International observers note the strategic significance of the Crimea energy strike, potentially influencing diplomatic discussions at the upcoming NATO summit.
sections.intelligence_notes: Monitoring of Shahed launch sites in Crimea, Bryansk and Donetsk is essential for early warning of inbound threats. UAV sightings over the Black Sea and near Odesa warrant increased maritime surveillance to protect naval assets. The relocation of a Tu‑160 bomber suggests possible preparation for long‑range cruise missile sorties, requiring radar and air‑defence readiness. Continued assessment of interceptor stockpiles is critical to address the identified shortfall in ballistic missile defence.
